app_documentation:
StudyCircle is a mobile-first web application (React front end, Node.js REST API, PostgreSQL database, JWT authentication, and AWS S3 file storage) that helps university students study together. Its purpose is to give students one place to share and find study notes and to form study groups around their courses. Students register with a verified university email, so the community stays limited to real students. It is intended for university students, group admins who run study groups, moderators who keep the platform safe, and platform administrators who manage the service.

The MVP has five features. Study Note Sharing (F1, High) lets students upload PDF or image notes of up to 20 MB with a title, university, course, and topic tags. They can search by keyword and filter by university, course, topic, and rating, with results ranked by relevance using PostgreSQL full-text search, and they can download notes. Study Groups (F2, High) lets students create public or private groups around a course or subject. Public groups can be joined directly. Private groups use a request flow in which the group admin approves or rejects requests and can remove members. User Authentication and Profiles (F3, High) covers registration with a university email, email-link verification, bcrypt password hashing, JWT login, and profile editing with bio, courses, and interests. Note Interaction and Feedback (F4, Medium) adds 1-5 star ratings with an immediately updated average, comments, and bookmarks. Moderation and Reporting (F5, Medium) lets users report notes or comments for reasons such as inappropriate content, copyright, or spam. Moderators then work a queue in which they remove content, notify the author, suspend users, or dismiss reports, with every action recorded in an audit log.

The design is a clean card-based interface with an indigo (#4F46E5) theme and Inter typography. It has a four-tab bottom navigation bar (Home, Groups, Upload, Profile) that becomes a left sidebar on desktop, with content capped at 1100px. The screens are Sign Up / Log In, Home - Browse Notes, Note Detail, Upload Note, Study Groups, Profile, and Moderation Queue, which is visible to moderators only. The design targets WCAG AA accessibility, 44px minimum touch targets, and reduced-motion support. The data model has 27 PostgreSQL tables covering universities, courses, topics, users, profiles, roles, notes and files, ratings, comments, bookmarks, groups, join requests, reports, moderation actions, notifications, and GDPR account deletion requests.

Non-functional commitments are: pages load in under 2 seconds and search returns in under 1 second at 500 concurrent users. All traffic uses HTTPS, and uploaded files are malware-scanned and held in a pending_scan state until clean. Monthly uptime is 99.5% excluding scheduled maintenance. Users can delete their account and personal data within 30 days, in line with GDPR, through a soft-delete followed by a purge job. The delivery plan (StudyCircle MVP Plan) has 14 tasks (T1-T14) covering schema, design system, scaffolding, authentication, upload and search, groups, feedback, moderation, GDPR deletion, and a final performance and QA pass. Key risks to track are malware scan integration, university domain allowlist maintenance and email deliverability, search performance at scale, abusive or copyrighted content before moderation ships, and overall scope for a small team.
baseline_artifacts: Requirements_v1 (5 features F1-F5, user stories, acceptance criteria, technical and non-functional requirements, 4 user roles)
Design_v1 (7 screens, indigo color scheme, Inter typography, bottom navigation, UI component library, accessibility and responsive guidelines)
Database_v1 (27-table PostgreSQL schema with uuid keys, indexes, relationships, and 16 documented assumptions)
CyclePlan_v1 (StudyCircle MVP Plan: tasks T1-T14 with dependencies, estimates, priorities, and 5 identified risks)

glossary.Study Note: A PDF or image file uploaded by a student, tagged with a university, course, and topic tags, that peers can search, download, rate, comment on, and bookmark. A note stays in pending_scan status until its files pass the malware scan.
glossary.Study Group: A public or private group that students create around a course or subject. Public groups can be joined directly. Private groups require a join request approved by the group admin.
glossary.Group Admin: A group-scoped role stored in group_members.role. It is given to a group's creator and lets them approve or reject join requests and remove members. It is distinct from the global roles Student, Moderator, and Platform Administrator.
glossary.Moderator: A global role that reviews reports in the Moderation Queue. Moderators can remove notes or comments, notify authors, suspend users, or dismiss reports, and every action is logged in the moderation_actions audit table.
glossary.University Email Verification: The process of confirming student status at registration. The email domain must match an entry in universities.email_domain, and the user must confirm a single-use, expiring verification link before the account changes from pending_verification to active.
glossary.GDPR Account Deletion: The workflow that lets users delete their account and personal data within 30 days. It is tracked in account_deletion_requests, soft-deletes the user first, then purges personal data, and deletes or anonymizes authored content by nulling the author, user, and reporter references.
